scenario: [LCRS.6.2.4]: a call fires twice under one correlation before either request is answered, so neither firing's own supersede ([LCRS.6.2.1]) finds a reply to retract. The host then asserts reply A (v 1) and reply B (v 2), both with corr `c1`. The arriving B retracts the live A before B is asserted, so exactly one reply is live, B's: `probe` fires once and logs ["live 2"]. PATH PINNED: the host-assert supersede -- `ds_dispatch_supersede_arrival` from `engine_assert_body` (libds) and `ds.exec.lcrs_6_2_4_arrival_victims` from `ds.engine.host_assert_unstamped` (Mercury) -- for a fact of a response schema. Not the call-side sweep: both calls fire before any reply exists. The break is an assert path with no arrival retraction: both replies stay live and `probe` logs twice.
rules_ds:
schema Reply scope ttl 1_h:
    corr: String
    v: Int

service svc.read:
    kwarg n: Int
    response Reply

schema Job scope explicit:
    id: Int

schema Probe scope explicit:
    k: Int

rule r:
    Job j
->
    call svc.read n: j.id nocooldown as "c1"

rule probe:
    Probe
    Reply x
->
    log info "live {x.v}"
